content.title: About
content.content: Water chestnut (Eleocharis dulcis) is an edible underground stem that grows in freshwater wetlands of East Asia. It has a crisp texture, mildly sweet flavor, and is commonly used in Asian cuisine in salads, soups, and stir‑fries.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Water chestnut is often called “earth apple” because of its round shape and crunchy texture.
It is cultivated in rice paddies and marshes, where the stems are harvested by hand.
In China the water chestnut symbolizes longevity and prosperity.
There are two main varieties: a larger one for frying and a smaller one for salads.
Fresh product can be kept in the refrigerator for up to a week, frozen for up to six months.

items.title: Low in calories
items.content: One hundred grams of water chestnut provides only about 30 kcal, making it a diet‑friendly snack.

items.title: Rich in fiber
items.content: Dietary fiber supports healthy digestion and promotes satiety.

items.title: Source of B‑vitamins
items.content: Contains thiamine, niacin, and folate, which are important for metabolism.

items.title: Contains minerals
items.content: Provides potassium, magnesium, and iron in modest amounts to help maintain electrolyte balance.

items.title: Antioxidant properties
items.content: Phenolic compounds may protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions, especially if they are sensitive to other sedge family plants.

items.title: Water‑borne contamination
items.content: Improperly processed chestnuts can harbor bacteria or parasites, so they should be thoroughly washed and cooked.

items.title: High sodium in canned form
items.content: Canned water chestnuts often contain added salt; people with hypertension should choose fresh or low‑sodium versions.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Fresh stems are peeled, the root end trimmed, and sliced. They can be added to salads, soups, stir‑fried until golden, or steamed. Canned water chestnuts are ready to eat straight from the jar.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store fresh water chestnuts in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 7 days. Canned chestnuts stay sealed in a cool, dry place until the expiration date. Frozen product should be kept at –18 °C for no more than 6 months.
